feature: The timeline of an hour-long edit: clips with pictures and the Music track are painted too
summary: On a long edit, clips that show pictures along them and sounds of their own (the Music track) are now painted as one layer per track instead of a view each, and a scroll slides that layer instead of painting it again. Zooming the hour-long edit near the whole-hour view went from about 92 ms a frame to 47, and a fast scroll from 27 ms to 17. The timeline looks the same.
setup: Photonz Probe built by Scripts/probe-app.sh, release Next, no flag changed from its default. The 60 minute reference edit: Scripts/perf/reference-edit.sh 60 (the 6 minute one shows the same pictures).

try.do: Open the 6 minute reference edit, press the zoom-in key four times so about 40 seconds show: the clips on V1 show their pictures, names in dark pills.
Compare with the same view on the build before this change: pictures, names, bands and waveforms in the same places.
Swipe along the timeline with two fingers: the pictures slide with their clips, and new ones fade in where you stop.
Open the 60 minute edit, scroll the tracks down to Music, and pinch the timeline in and out near the whole-hour view.
Rest the pointer on a Music clip, then on a V1 clip with pictures: each becomes its full bar under the pointer, grips and fade diamonds live.
Click a Music clip without moving the pointer first, then drag it along: it picks and moves like any clip.
Press Fit: the whole edit, exactly as before.

evaluate: Does pinching the hour-long edit near the whole-hour view feel noticeably smoother than before?
When you stop a fast swipe, do the pictures along the clips fill in quickly enough?
Does the Music track look exactly as it did (name tag, waveform, level line, fade diamonds)?
Does a picture fading in as it lands look right, or would you rather it simply appeared?
measured: Speed walk timeline measure on the 60 minute reference edit (524 clips: 378 on V1, 70 on V2, 53 Music, 22 titles), markers down, 120 Hz. Before is 55839469c, measured today on the same Mac.
Zoom in: median 41.7 ms a frame before (p95 203), 24.9 after (p95 67). Zoom out: 42.3 (p95 221) before, 24.8 (p95 67) after.

By zoom (new in the speed walk's line, the median frame at each doubling): near the whole-hour view 1x 92 to 110 ms before, 43 to 47 after; 8x 66 to 75 before, 47 to 51 after; 256x and further in 17 before and after (14 to 17).
Scroll end to end in three seconds, half a minute on screen: median 41.5 ms (p95 50) before, 17.0 (p95 33) after.
Edits (longest main thread pass): trim 108 to 64 ms, move 102 to 49, blade 162 to 100, undo 122 to 76, transition 174 to 117, title 84 to 42.
Playing untouched: 104 to 106 pictures in 3 s, no clip bar built per picture, before and after.
rough: The bars of the task are still not reached: 8.3 ms a frame for zoom and scroll, 16 ms for an edit. Measured by taking parts out on a throwaway build: what is left near the whole-hour view is mostly the 22 titles (a quiet track, still a view each) and the cuts; all of them out, a zoom frame there is 19 ms and a scroll frame 8.3.
A painted picture that lands fades in over a fifth of a second like a full bar's, but the name tag over a strip that comes in with a zoom does not fade with it.

Pixel check against the build before: Fit is identical; zoomed in, about 1 percent of the timeline's pixels differ, at the edges of pictures and the antialiasing of the names. On the older build several pictures had not landed after 3 s where the new one shows them all.

Found and fixed on the way: a busy lane's sound halves each made an empty item in a list, every clip in sight carried a click tick view with no clicks, and finding whether a clip carries its sound went through the whole track for every clip; each cost a few ms near the whole-hour view.
